Roofing in Humble, TX

A Humble address can mean the old oil town, a Lake Houston subdivision or a street inside another city. The rules for your roof follow the city line. Call one free number at any hour to reach an independent, locally owned roofer.

Call (832) 662-4107 Which rules apply to you

An oil town with a big mailing address

Roofing in Humble, TX means different paperwork depending on which Humble you live in. The city is small and old. The Humble mailing address wraps around it and reaches far more households than the city itself, most of them outside its limits.

The city's own history traces the name to Pleasant Humble. His ferry crossed the San Jacinto close to where US 59 spans the river today, and in 1886 he opened a post office in his home, which is when the Humble name was adopted. Oil changed everything early in the next century. By 1905 the Humble field was the largest producing oil field in Texas, the oil company that later became part of Exxon was named Humble after the town, and the city incorporated in 1933.

That history is still visible in the housing. Streets near the old townsite hold the oldest houses, while newer subdivisions spread out toward Lake Houston and the river. An old house and a new one call for different conversations with a roofer, and the section below explains why.

Houston Expert Roofers does not inspect, repair or replace roofs. The number costs nothing to call. An automated assistant collects a short account of the problem and your location, then connects you with an independent, locally owned roofing company working in Humble, which visits, writes up its own estimate, carries out the job and is paid by you.

Sorting out a Humble address before you sign anything

Who issues the permit, who you call about a downed line and which rules the roofer has to follow all depend on the jurisdiction, not the envelope. Work through it in this order.

  1. Check your tax statement. Your property tax bill or appraisal district record lists each taxing unit on your land. If it names the City of Humble, you are inside the city.
  2. Inside the City of Humble. The city's building inspection office issues building permits and has an online permit portal, though not every permit can be filed there. Ask the roofer whether your re-roof needs a city permit, and if it does, have the company pull it in its own name and show it to you before tear-off. Do not rely on a fee you read somewhere; ask the city for the current one.
  3. In unincorporated Harris County. Much of the area around Humble, including Atascocita, has no city government. There is no city roofing permit and no city inspector. Outside any city, the Harris County engineer's office is the permit authority, and its permits mostly concern development and the floodplain; call it if you are unsure. On a county re-roof, the written contract and the roofer's photos are your record.
  4. Across the river in Kingwood. Kingwood is part of the City of Houston, which requires a residential roofing permit for a re-roof or overlay. If your house is there, read the Kingwood page.

A roofing company that works the Humble area should ask which of these applies in the first conversation. If one says no permit is ever needed anywhere around Humble, it does not know the area.

Older Humble houses: what a roofer may find under the shingles

A house near the original townsite has usually been re-roofed more than once. Each time, someone decided whether to tear off the old layer or lay new shingles over it, and whether to replace tired decking. You inherit those decisions. These are the things worth asking about before you accept a price.

A second layer

Shingles laid over old shingles add weight, hide rot and shorten the life of the new roof, because the top layer cannot lie flat. Ask whether your roof has more than one layer and price a full tear-off to the deck.

Plank decking

Many older homes were built with board decking rather than plywood sheets. Gaps between boards can be too wide for modern shingle nailing. A roofer may recommend new sheathing over the planks; ask why and what it costs per sheet.

Little or no attic ventilation

Older attics often have a couple of small vents and nothing else. In a Gulf Coast summer that bakes shingles from below. A replacement is the natural time to add ridge and soffit vents, while the deck is open, so ask what the roofer plans.

Newer homes in the subdivisions around Humble have different weak points: complex rooflines with several valleys, pipe boots and flashing that age faster than the shingles, and builder-grade materials reaching the end of their life all at once on the same street. The roof lifespan guide explains how long Houston-area roofs usually last.

Harvey, the river and Humble roofs

The San Jacinto's West Fork passes Humble before it widens into Lake Houston. During Harvey in late August 2017, Community Impact Newspaper reported the river gauge at US 59 in Humble at 62 feet and still forecast to rise. Local estimates later cited in the City of Houston's dredging updates put the Harvey toll around the lake at upward of 16,000 homes and roughly 3,300 businesses.

Floods are not roof events, but they leave roof questions behind. Houses that took water were gutted and rebuilt in a hurry, and the attic was rarely the priority. If your house flooded, ask the roofer to look at the attic for old water stains, mold on the underside of the decking and any ceiling joists that were cut or patched during the rebuild.

Two more recent storms hit the whole region. The National Weather Service office in League City documented the May 16, 2024 derecho, and Hurricane Beryl on July 8, 2024 knocked out power to more than two million CenterPoint Energy customers. Both lifted shingles and dropped limbs across greater Houston, so a roof in Humble that has not been looked at since then is worth checking if you see a new stain.

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to CenterPoint Energy or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

Why Humble homeowners call the line

A leak on a house that has been patched before

On an older roof with years of repairs, a new drip can come from any of them. Callers want a roofer who will trace the water in the attic rather than add another dab of roofing cement on top of the last one.

A whole street of roofs the same age

When a subdivision is built in a few years, its roofs wear out together. Once a few neighbors replace theirs, other owners start asking whether theirs is next. A roofer with photos from your own roof answers that better than the neighbors can.

Pines and pine straw

Humble is wooded, and pine needles pile up in valleys and gutters and hold water against the flashing. Shaded slopes grow dark algae streaks. Neither is an emergency, but both shorten a roof's life if nobody deals with them.

Not knowing whose rules apply

City of Humble, unincorporated county or City of Houston: the answer changes the paperwork. Callers want a company that already works on their side of the line and does not have to guess.

Before you hire a Humble roofer, ask

  • Is my house inside the City of Humble, and does this job need a city permit? Who pulls it?
  • How many layers of shingles are on the roof now, and is your price for a full tear-off?
  • Is my decking plank or plywood, and what do you charge per sheet if some has to be replaced?
  • What ventilation will the new roof have at the ridge and soffits?
  • Can you send a certificate of liability insurance with my name on it?
  • What is your workmanship warranty, in writing, and how do I register the shingle maker's warranty?
  • If this is an insurance job, will your contract carry the deductible notice Texas law requires?

Any insurance claim is filed by you, with your insurer. The roofer can document damage, but under Texas law it may not act as your public adjuster on a house it works on.

How a Humble call works

  1. Call the numberAn automated assistant answers (832) 662-4107 at any hour and asks which service you need, since the line also takes heating, cooling, pressure washing and water damage calls.
  2. Describe the roofA leak, missing shingles, hail, a limb on the roof or an old roof you want looked at, plus your part of greater Houston and how urgent it is.
  3. Get put throughYour call is transferred to an independent, locally owned roofing company, which hears a short summary before it picks up.
  4. Deal with the roofer directlyIt inspects, quotes and does the work, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it misses the call, it gets your name, number, city and need to call you back.

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Is a permit required for a new roof in Humble, Texas?

It depends on where the house is. Inside the City of Humble, the city's building inspection office handles building permits and runs an online permit portal (not every permit type can be filed online), so ask the city or your roofer what a re-roof at your address needs and have the roofer pull it in its own name. If your Humble address is in unincorporated Harris County, no city roofing permit exists; permits on county land come from the Harris County engineer's office. The address section shows how to tell.

Is Atascocita part of Humble?

No. Atascocita uses Humble mailing addresses, but it has never been part of the city; the Handbook of Texas gives it its own entry as a community in northeastern Harris County, so City of Humble rules do not reach it. Kingwood, across the river's West Fork, is different again: it is inside the City of Houston. Each has its own page: Atascocita and Kingwood.

My Humble house flooded in Harvey. Does that matter for a new roof?

It can. Flood repairs often replaced drywall and insulation but left the attic alone, and a roof that leaked during the same storm may have been patched in a hurry. Tell the roofer the house took water in 2017 and ask it to check the attic decking and ceiling joists. Remember that flood and wind are different insurance policies; the insurance claims guide explains roof claims.

Can roofers in Humble, TX show me a state license?

No, because Texas does not license roofing contractors. A bill in 2025 to create a license did not pass. Instead, ask for a certificate of liability insurance made out to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where the city requires one, and addresses of recent roofs near Humble you can drive past. The guide to checking a roofer has the full list.

Who answers when I call about roofing in Humble?

The free line's automated assistant picks up day or night, notes the roof problem and your part of the Humble area, then puts the call through to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Humble calls. The inspection, the quote and the roof work all belong to that company, and you settle the bill with it, not with the line. Houston Expert Roofers never climbs a roof, and companies may pay it a referral fee.
